dek: An Ohio pick service in business since 1982, home of the Power Sweep and Power Plays football newsletters. Season subscriptions start at $69 to $89, and single night plays sell for about $15. The BBB rates it A+ with no complaints, while a long running forum tracker reports losing seasons for its rated plays.

short_answer: Northcoast Sports is a real and very old business. Its site gives a street address, a toll free number and office hours, and the Better Business Bureau lists Northcoast Sports Service as accredited since 2000 with an A+ rating, a start date of 1982 and Phil Steele as owner. A 2007 Cleveland Scene profile described it as Phil Steele's business. In that sense it is legitimate.

What it sells is mostly football. Power Sweep and Power Plays are weekly newsletters with previews, projected box scores and star rated plays. Late phone packages sell star rated, Marquee and Game of the Month plays by the day, and the Community Line resells plays from other handicappers. The site claims its free Early Bird Play of the Week has "produced 62% Winners OVER 28 YEARS," but we found no full log of those plays.

Independent evidence comes mostly from one TheRX member who tracked the rated plays for several seasons and reported net losses after service costs. Other members said they do well picking among the plays. Prices are low for the newsletters, so if you buy, start with one season and grade every play yourself.

guarantee: We found no guarantee, refund or credit wording on the homepage, the product pages, the free plays page or the FAQ. The FAQ covers only how and when newsletters are delivered.
A buyer should assume there is no money back if the plays lose. Losses on the bets themselves are never covered, and over a season they can be much larger than the price of a newsletter.

claims_note: The 62% figure covers one free play a week over 28 years. That is a small slice of what Northcoast sells, and the site does not show the list of plays behind it.
The Community Line resells other services, including one sold under the Jim Feist name. Any record shown there belongs to those services, not to Northcoast's own handicapping.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: Northcoast keeps an archive of past Power Sweep and Power Plays issues going back to 2010, so newsletter plays can in principle be graded from the issues. We did not grade them. We found no public, time stamped log of the late phone plays.
What the site publishes: ATS logs of every college and NFL game with lines and results, which are schedule data rather than a record of Northcoast picks, and the 62% claim for its free weekly play.

What a forum tracker reports: one TheRX member posted weekly records of the rated plays for several seasons. For 2023 he reported college sides and totals at 63 wins, 89 losses and 6 pushes and the NFL at 38, 36 and 3, with service costs of $4,624. Late in 2024 he reported college sides at 41 and 43, totals at 31 and 29, and the NFL at 32, 36 and 1. These are one person's counts, not an audit.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no Northcoast Sports pick history is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how Northcoast performs.
our_data.context: For scale: the site claims 62% winners on its free weekly play. On the Watchdog board, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent evidence on Northcoast Sports sits almost entirely on TheRX forum, where members share and track its plays, plus a BBB profile and one Covers post. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We read about ten posts from 2023 to 2025 on TheRX and Covers, plus the BBB profile. The most detailed evidence is a TheRX thread, started in August 2023, in which one member tracked the rated plays week by week and reported losing seasons once service costs were added. Other members in the same thread said the Game of the Month and Game of the Year plays often win and that they profit by choosing among the plays. A separate thread said the newsletters were losing subscribers while prices rose. The BBB shows no complaints in three years. Most of the negative numbers come from a single tracker, so they are one person's view, but they cover several seasons.

The TheRX tracker posted his final 2023 counts: college sides and totals 63 wins, 89 losses, 6 pushes, college sides alone 40 and 66, and NFL 38 and 36. He put service costs at $4,624 and said a $100 a play bettor following the scale would be down about $13,990. Earlier that week he said the Executive Service for the NFL playoffs was cut from $500 to $345.

The same tracker listed the 2023 Power Sweep star plays: college 4 star at 5 wins and 11 losses, 3 star at 15 and 20, and NFL 3 star at 4 and 13. He called the newsletter plays worthless and said the staff never mention their record.

In a TheRX newsletters thread, a member said Northcoast controls Power Sweep, Power Plays and Phil Steele's releases, and that these publications were losing subscribers while raising prices. Another member's tracking post in the thread showed most Power Sweep and Power Plays star levels below 50% for the season to date.
A TheRX member said he does well with Northcoast plays by adding his own research and money management, and that the star rated Power Sweep and late phone plays are usually good.

The tracker reported 2024 season to date college sides at 25 and 26, totals at 15 and 21, and NFL at 18 and 19, with service costs of $2,983 and a $100 bettor down $7,124. He also said he complained to Northcoast about a $10 price rise for the weekly publications.

Several TheRX members said Northcoast's Game of the Month and Game of the Year plays are usually strong. Days later a member noted the Game of the Year won but the other rated plays lost, and the tracker reported the NFL at 32, 36 and 1 for the season with service costs of $4,772 so far.

A TheRX post quoted the tracker saying that a client who followed the ratings at $100 a unit was down $9,600, while answering another member who had praised the late phone plays. This is a forum claim we could not check.
On Covers, a bettor said he uses Northcoast newsletters alongside two other newsletters. A reply called such newsletters losing publications in general, without naming Northcoast.

The BBB profile for Northcoast Sports Service showed an A+ rating, accreditation since 22 Nov 2000, zero complaints in the last three years and zero customer reviews. We found no news report, court record or regulator action about the service.

conflicts: The Community Line page resells plays from other services, including one under the Jim Feist name. Northcoast earns from those sales, so its listing of them as top rated is not independent.
TheRX members regularly post Northcoast's paid plays in public threads. That makes the plays easy to track, but it also means the tracker's records depend on what members chose to post.
strengths: A named owner, a street address, a toll free number and office hours, with BBB accreditation since 2000 and no complaints there in three years.
Newsletter prices are low and published, with cheaper prices for future seasons.
Past newsletter issues are archived on the site, so buyers can check old plays themselves.
Free weekly plays let you watch the service before paying.
concerns: No full public record of the late phone plays, which are where most of the money is spent.
A forum tracker reported losing seasons for the rated plays in 2023 and 2024 once service costs were counted.
No guarantee or refund wording that we could find.
The 62% claim covers only one free play a week and shows no list behind it.
checklist: Ask for every late phone play from the last season with the line, the star rating and the result. A free play record is not the paid record.
Count units, not wins. Higher star plays carry bigger stakes, so a few losses there cost more.
Add the price of the plays to your results. Several hundred dollars of service can erase a small winning edge.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: It is a real, long running business with a street address, a phone line and BBB accreditation since 2000, with no BBB complaints in three years. We could not verify that its plays win over time, because it does not publish a full record of its paid plays.
How much does Northcoast Sports cost?

On 16 Nov 2026 a 2026 season of Power Sweep or Power Plays by email cost $89.00, with the second newsletter $50.00 more, and later seasons cheaper. The Monday Night NFL Marquee cost $15.00 for one day. Other daily packages showed no live price.
Does Northcoast Sports have a verified record?

No. The site claims 62% winners over 28 years on its free weekly play and archives old newsletters, but we found no independent log of every paid play. A forum tracker reported losing seasons in 2023 and 2024.

The newsletters are cheap and full of football information, and some bettors say they use them as a starting point. What is unproven is whether the paid plays beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 after the cost of the service, and nothing refunds the package or your betting losses.
